I live in Denver, and use Uber almost every time I go out.

I used Uber shortly after its launch in San Francisco, and I remember when it added "UberX" and eventually rebranded its original service to "Uber Black." I've also used Uber abroad in cities like Paris and Panama City.

The experience varies.

At first, it was amazing but also more expensive: A professional driver, usually wearing a suit, would pull up in a Lincoln Town Car, open the door for you as you walked up to the curb, and take you silently where you needed to go as you sipped bottled water. That experience still party exists with Uber Black, but I would say the standard of professionalism has slipped a bit; sometimes the drivers will not have water, the vehicles aren't as clean as they were, and the drivers somewhat less professional at times (I had to ask one to turn down his shitty music lately).

That's Uber Black.

Uber X/XL and Lyft, unlike Uber Black, do not hire professionally trained livery drivers. Uber X and Lyft drivers are just typical people in their regular personal cars, which range considerably. Their professionalism and driving competence do vary, with some actually being unfamiliar with the cities they operate in. Lyft even encourages drivers to basically become your friend, and that's a little irritating if you really just want to be shuttled where you're going. Uber also offers Uber Select, which has nicer vehicles that aren't "livery" vehicles. For example, a BMW 5 series is typical of Uber Select.

Also keep in mind that for both Uber and Lyft, different services are available in different cities. In Denver, you have everything from Uber Black SUV to Uber X, Uber Select, and so on. In contrast, only Uber Black was available in much of Latin America, and Uber X is only available in some places I've been to.
Can't speak for Lyft, but Uber was fast + you don't need to worry about the driver taking a roundabout path in order to run up the meter.

Uber is pretty much my go-to way to get around town when I'm going out. Don't have to deal with parking or figuring out directions and no one in your group is forced to be DD. Sometimes the driver is talkative, sometimes not. In general drivers are pretty laid back, respectful, and don't push and boundries. I've never had an overly negative experience that would keep me from using Uber again.
I have used it in Seattle, Portland, and Los Angeles. Worlds better than taxi's. You don't get treated like you're a piece of shit when you take an Uber or a Lyft.

I live in Los Angeles and almost exclusively use Lyft at this point. They offer an identical service to Uber, with generally younger/friendlier drivers who are more up for a chat. Additionally, Uber implements "surge pricing" during peak hours which can get as high as 800% more than the ride would normally be. Lyft does something similar, but I've never seen it exceed 100%.

At this point, Uber is a massive corporation and is starting to exhibit some signs of corporate shiftiness/greed. While I'm sure Lyft will end up doing similar things, for the moment I think they are the far better and more cost-effective choice.
